sections.h2: What towns and landmarks make up Greene County?
sections.html:
Greene County is in east central Georgia, in the part of the state known as the Lake country, and Greensboro is the county seat and largest city. The legislature formed it on February 3, 1786, from land taken from Washington County, and it carries the name of Revolutionary War general Nathanael Greene (Wikipedia).

Of the county's 406 square miles, 387 are land and 19, or 4.6%, are water. Rivers drain it three ways: the Oconee River in the west, the Little River toward the Savannah in the north, and the Ogeechee in the south. Part of the Oconee National Forest lies inside the boundary, and the extinct river town of Scull Shoals marks its earlier history. Interstate 20 crosses the county alongside US 278 and State Routes 12, 15, 44 and 77.

Incorporated places are Greensboro, Union Point, White Plains and Woodville, plus the town of Siloam. Bairdstown is an unincorporated community. Oglethorpe, Taliaferro, Hancock, Putnam, Morgan and Oconee counties surround it. Families here choose among the Greene County School Board, Lake Oconee Academy and Nathanael Greene Academy. If you hold a lakeside or in-town parcel, the county tax commissioner still sends the bill, so the steps below apply wherever the house stands.

sections.h2: What do Greene County's Census figures show for homeowners?
sections.html:
Greene County grew from 18,915 people in the 2020 census to an estimated 21,367 in July 2025, a gain of 13.0%. Residents 65 and older make up 33.5% of the population, a full third, so the senior exemptions listed further down apply to a large share of local owners. Wikipedia links recent growth to people moving to Reynolds Lake Oconee.

sections.h2: Where do Greene County property tax questions go?
sections.html:
Both offices share the building at 1034 Silver Drive in Greensboro. The tax commissioner bills and collects tax on real and personal property, mobile homes, motor vehicles, timber and utilities, and also issues vehicle tags as an agent for the state. The tax assessors set values, take returns and approve exemptions.

  • Tax Commissioner: Suite 101, 1034 Silver Drive, Greensboro, GA 30642, phone 706-453-3358, lobby open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 4:45 pm.
  • Tax Assessors: Suite 102 of the same address, phone 706-453-3355, handling values, appeals and homestead filings.
  • Online: the county posts a homestead application page and a digest and assessments page for the current year.

The commissioner's page and the assessors' appeal page are the official sources for hours and forms.

sections.h2: When is Greene County property tax due?
sections.html:
December 1 is the due date for property tax in Greene County, and it moves to the next business day when it lands on a weekend or holiday. The commissioner's page warns that property on which tax is left unpaid may be levied upon and eventually sold.

The calendar around that date runs on a fixed pattern. Taxpayers file a return for property they own on January 1, and returns are accepted from January 1 through April 1. A real property return renews itself each year at the previous value, but personal property needs a new return every year. Mobile homes follow their own rule: under the state's county facts sheet, an owner returns the home for tax by April 1 and applies for the annual location permit between January 1 and April 1. Assessment notices usually go out around May, and millage rates are set later in the year by the commissioners and the school board.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Greene County assessment?
sections.html:
A property owner has 45 days from the date the notice was mailed to appeal. The appeal can rest on taxability, value, uniformity or the denial of an exemption, and it goes in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors on the state's uniform form, PT-311A. Your first letter has to name the route you want.

  • Board of Equalization: the assessors review first and may send an amended notice, which you can appeal within 30 days; any appeal they leave unchanged moves on to the Board of Equalization for a hearing, and Superior Court is the next step.
  • Hearing officer: a certified appraiser decides value disputes, but only for non-homestead real property worth $1,000,000 or more.
  • Arbitration: you submit a current certified appraisal, the assessors may accept or reject it, and a rejected one goes to the clerk of Superior Court. A hearing follows within 30 days, and the arbitrator's decision is final.

The county's own page reads this out in full, and it says the appeal forms are on the Department of Revenue's website.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Greene County use?
sections.html:
To get the exemption for a given year you must have owned and lived in the home on January 1 and filed by April 1, and later filings wait for the next year. Once granted it renews each year until ownership, residence or exemption type changes. The county's chart lists these deductions from assessed value:

  • S1, state default: $2,000, applied to county and school taxes.
  • L1, age 65 and over: $10,000, which the county explains as $2,000 state plus $8,000 local.
  • S3, ages 62 to 64 with net income of $10,000 at most: $2,000 for county taxes and $10,000 for school taxes.
  • L4, age 65 and over with net income of $10,000 at most: $12,000 for county taxes and $18,000 for school taxes.
  • S5 and L5, 100% disabled veteran or unremarried surviving spouse: $100,896, a 2021 state figure that changes annually and requires proof.

An F added to any code, such as S1F, marks the homestead freeze, which exempts increases in assessed value above the level on the day the exemption was approved. The county says it covers the house and up to five acres, and excludes pools, barns, detached garages and shops (county homestead page). The county also describes a deferral program for owners 62 and older with household income of $15,000 or less, and preferential assessment at 30% for qualifying farmland.

sections.h2: What should a Greene County seller do about tax before closing?
sections.html:
The Georgia Department of Revenue says that if you owned a property on January 1, you are responsible for the entire year's tax even if you sell on January 2, and there is no refund for part of a year. A purchase contract usually splits the bill, so the figure that matters is the exact balance on the parcel.

Ask the commissioner's office for a statement of what is owed for the present and prior years. If the sale falls close to December 1, ask which amount the closing agent should wire. Keep your assessment notice and any appeal paperwork with the file, because a pending appeal can change the final bill. Tell the assessors in writing when you move out, so your homestead code comes off the property and the new owner can apply under their own name.

faqs.q: When is the Greene County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: December 1 is the due date, or the next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday. The tax commissioner's page also says unpaid property may be levied upon and eventually sold.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to appeal in Greene County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the day the assessment notice was mailed. File a written appeal with the Board of Tax Assessors and say whether you want the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer or arbitration.

faqs.q: What is the Greene County homestead filing deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 is the deadline for the current tax year, and you must have owned and lived in the home on January 1. A later application is held until the following year.

faqs.q: What is the Greene County homestead freeze?
faqs.a: It is an exemption equal to any rise in assessed value above the value on the date your homestead was approved, shown as an F after the code, for example S1F. The county says it applies to the home and up to five acres but not to pools, barns, detached garages or shops.

faqs.q: Who do I call in Greene County about tax bills and values?
faqs.a: Call the tax commissioner at 706-453-3358 for bills and payments, and the tax assessors at 706-453-3355 for values, appeals and exemptions. Both are at 1034 Silver Drive in Greensboro.
